html:
The Quillacinga were an Indigenous people of the highlands of southern Colombia, around the valley where the city of Pasto now stands and the lake of La Cocha. Their name is often explained as Quechua for "moon nose", after the crescent nose ornaments they wore.

Little is known of their language, which is extinct and unclassified. Their neighbours to the south were the Pastos. The northern edge of the Inca Empire reached this region under Huayna Capac in the early 1500s, though how far Inca rule went here is disputed. Spaniards founded Pasto in the late 1530s, divided the Quillacinga among encomienda holders, and over the colonial centuries they merged into the wider population of Spanish America.
